Admission Policies and Requirements
Admission Policies and Requirements
Download as PDF
Applicants to graduate programs in the College of Liberal Arts and Science are admitted wholly on individual merit. Villanova University does not discriminate against anyone seeking admission on the basis of their race, color, national or ethnic origin, religion, or sex.
Applicants should review the general admissions policies below and explore the web pages of the program of interest for further information about application deadlines, admissions criteria, curriculum requirements, course offerings, resources for students and other discipline-specific details. Please also review application deadlines for each program.
The Office of Graduate Studies also offers additional resources for current teachers, military and veterans, and international students.
General Admissions Policies
Bachelor’s Degree
All applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an institution accredited by one of the regional accrediting agencies prior to enrollment in our graduate degree and certificate programs.
Transcripts
Unofficial transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions you have attended and earned 10 or more credits (or the equivalent, if your institution's standard courses are not 3 credits each) are required at time of application. Official transcripts are required after an admission decision has been rendered and before a student can enroll in classes.
If the applicant has completed any program for which a transcript is required, the transcript must list the conferred degree and the conferral date.
Any applicant in their last year of undergraduate study at the time of application should provide a transcript of all courses completed to date including any in-progress courses ahead of graduation.
If admitted and intending to enroll, final official transcripts must be submitted to the Graduate Studies Office listing the degree received and the date the degree was conferred.
Pre-Requisites
All applicants must have completed the undergraduate prerequisites for graduate study in their proposed program. These prerequisites are detailed on each program’s admission requirements page.
Non-Matriculated and Visitor Applications
Applicants who wish to apply as non-matriculated (non-degree seeking) or visiting students must contact the Office of Graduate Studies to request the application link. Please email gradinformation@villanova.edu in order to apply. See more information on Student Status Categories.
VU Staff Admissions
VU staff are welcome to apply for our degrees and certificates! HR offers tuition remission to employees for graduate-level education, so take advantage of this amazing opportunity.
Application Requirement Waiver Requests
You will find a waiver request form in your application. Keep in mind that all waivers are subject to review and approval by Office of Graduate Studies admissions staff and internal waiver criteria.
We do not accept or approve Credential Evaluation waivers for international applicants.
Deadlines
View updated admission deadline dates.
Deferral Requests
Applicants who receive written notice of matriculated admission who cannot enroll in the admission cycle in which they were admitted, for whatever reason, may request a deferral via form submission. Applicants may defer once and subsequently extend that deferral once for a maximum of two admission cycles. No additional deferrals will be granted, but we are happy to support reapplication to the program.
Non-matriculated applicants cannot defer their admission, nor can international applicants who still need to submit financial certification.
This policy only applies to applicants who never officially started the program. For policy related to students who were previously enrolled, see Readmission.
NOTE: If you wish to change to a later term within the same calendar year (e.g., spring 2027 to summer 2027), reach out to the admissions counselor in your application portal.
Deferred Enrollment Confirmation
Applicants must confirm with the Office of Graduate Studies that they are prepared to enroll in their chosen deferral term at least two months prior to the start of that semester by completing our Deferred Enrollment Confirmation form. This form will be made available as the semester approaches.
Applicants deferring to the fall semester who would like to be considered for funding must complete the Deferred Enrollment Confirmation form in advance of the funding deadline for their specific program.

GRE is optional
Villanova’s graduate programs in the liberal arts and sciences use a holistic application review process, seeking to take into account each applicant’s individual qualifications and varied circumstances, and understanding that no single set of standards can fit every applicant equally well. Master of Arts in Communication
Application Requirements:
Online application form
Transcripts
3 recommendation letters
Resume/CV
Academic or professional writing sample: Please submit one solo-authored academic or professional writing sample. Please do not submit co-authored work unless your individual contribution can be clearly separated and identified.
The writing sample should demonstrate your ability to write clearly, organize ideas, develop an argument or analysis, and communicate effectively for an academic or professional audience. Appropriate samples may include, but are not limited to, an academic paper written for a class, conference, or journal; an academic report written for a class project, consulting project, or public relations campaign; a news article or feature story written for a publication or media outlet; or a professional report, memo, white paper, or similar document written for work.
In addition to the writing sample, please include a brief description of no more than 150 words. The description should explain the context or purpose of the piece, such as where or why it was written, the audience it was intended for, and how it demonstrates your academic and/or professional writing ability.
Statement of Goals
Your Statement of Goals should be no more than three double-spaced pages, using 12-point font. It should help the admissions committee understand your preparation for graduate study, your reasons for applying to Villanova University’s M.A. in Communication program, and the contributions you hope to make as a member of our graduate community. Rather than responding to each question separately, please write a coherent essay that addresses the following areas:
Describe your academic interests, professional aspirations, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in Communication. What academic, professional, research, creative, leadership, service, or other experiences have prepared you for the demands of graduate-level work?
Describe one or more ways you have engaged with a community that matters to you. This may include service, advocacy, leadership, mentoring, professional work, research, creative practice, civic participation, or other forms of community involvement. How has this engagement shaped your perspective, and how might it inform your participation in a graduate program that values rigorous intellectual work, professional development, and community-engaged learning?
Why are you interested in Villanova’s graduate program in Communication? Please discuss how the program’s curriculum, faculty, and applied learning opportunities may help you achieve your goals, and how you hope to contribute to the intellectual, professional, and community life of the graduate program. You may also use the statement to provide any relevant context about your application, including challenges, interruptions, or circumstances that affected your academic or professional record.
GRE/GMAT Optional:
Applicants are not required to submit GRE/GMAT scores as part of the application for the Master’s Degree in Communication. Applicants may submit GRE/ GMAT results, if they feel the scores enhance their application. If scores are submitted by an applicant, they will be reviewed as part of the admission review process. Applicants who do not submit scores will not be put at a disadvantage. If an applicant chooses to submit scores, they must follow up any self-reported scores with official test results.
$50 non-refundable application fee

In a cohesive statement no longer than 3 pages with 1.5 spacing, please describe:

Finally, if you wish to discuss lived experiences and other barriers that might have impacted your academic performance and professional experience, you may include a brief paragraph at the end of your statement to describe those factors.
Your statement will help us determine the fit between your interests and our program and also the fit between our program’s strengths and your eventual goals.
